Tier 2: Add a causal SASRec history encoder to the current attentive-similarity model. The latest model achieved macro validation HR@10 of 0.4313 versus the SASRec baseline’s 0.505, with particularly large deficits on Movies_and_TV and Electronics. This suggests that candidate-conditioned similarity and recency buckets may be losing useful interaction-order information, although the results do not establish the cause conclusively.

The primary component to modify is model_design: pass history embeddings through positional embeddings and two causal self-attention blocks before the existing candidate-conditioned attention pooling. Use a residual connection from the original history embeddings so the model can retain direct item similarity while learning contextual representations. Mask padding and future positions explicitly, and preserve chronological ordering in the existing sampled prefixes. Keep the sampled cross-entropy objective, negatives, optimizer, and training schedule unchanged to isolate this architectural addition.

The second component is training_evaluation: select checkpoints using validation HR@10 with the fixed 200-user, 99-unique-negative protocol and evaluation seed 42, then report the macro-average across all four categories. Update the predictor writer to reconstruct the contextual encoder and load its learned weights strictly, using identical history processing during validation and host inference. Preserve the supplied splits, DATA_DIR, dataset routing, and trial-local artifacts; leave hidden-test prediction generation to the host evaluator.
